off_spec_policy: UOP jet-focused design with light-olefin recycling and separate diesel, naphtha and residual streams
carbon_mass_fraction_status: Representative composition assumptions, not UOP measurements. Distinct from carbon-to-jet yield.
coproduct_scaling: Diesel and naphtha masses per kg pure methanol use their Table 2 output divided by 1200 * 0.9985. Jet alone is recalculated at the user-selected 85% carbon yield. This adapted slate is not an exact UOP plant reproduction.
coproduct_use_policy: User-approved fuel use: diesel and naphtha fully combust one year after production. Matching avoided upstream fossil production and combustion CO2 are credited in the production year. No petrochemical naphtha pool or allocation.

coproduct_combustion.counterfactual_basis: Equal-mass, composition-equivalent fossil fuel. The existing representative carbon mass fraction (0.85) applies to both synthetic and displaced fuel; this is a webinar equivalence assumption, not a measured fuel specification.

residual_policy: User-approved aggregate closure: upstream methanol residual and methanol-to-X residual are released as non-fossil CO2 in the production year. This is a webinar modelling assumption, not a quantified fate reported by UOP. No heat credit.
uop_process_boundary: Methanol feed through olefin production, concentration and fractionation, oligomerization, hydrogenation and product fractionation. Upstream CO2-to-methanol synthesis is outside this patent model.
uop_recycle: Unconverted ethylene and propylene return to olefin concentration/fractionation. C4-C8 olefins recycle to oligomerization. Internal recycle is not an additional carbon input or a substitution credit.

uop_residual_streams.description: Waste gas containing light paraffins, hydrogen and CO
Saturated light gas containing hydrogen and C1-C4 paraffins
uop_residual_streams.fate: Patent permits use as fuel gas, without quantifying the heat recovered

uop_residual_streams.description: Carbon-containing treatment streams, including oxygenate-rich water and CO2-rich spent caustic in optional configurations
uop_residual_streams.fate: Configuration-dependent, quantities and treatment not specified by Table 2

residual_heat_credit_status: No credit pending a quantified process energy balance, not an assertion that heat recovery is absent
release_blockers: Rebase operating energy and hydrogen to the recycled multi-output design
status: user-selected literature-supported candidate design, incomplete for LCIA release
interpretation: 85% is methanol carbon retained in jet. Diesel and naphtha are additional physical products drawn from the remaining carbon. The balance remainder stays explicit. This is a simulation-informed assumption, not measured industrial performance.

sources.citation: UOP LLC, US20260098223A1, Table 2, improved light-gas-recycle configuration (2026)
sources.support: UniSim process simulation reports 85.4% methanol-carbon yield to SAF, plus 7.9 kt/year diesel and 15.6 kt/year naphtha from 1200 kt/year methanol feed at 99.85 wt% purity. The webinar retains 85%.

sources.citation: Elwaily et al. (2025), Sustainable aviation fuel production via the methanol pathway: a technical review
sources.support: Integrated methanol-to-jet concepts require recycle streams and process integration to improve jet-fuel yield.

sources.citation: Fraunhofer ISE SAFari methanol-to-jet process development
sources.support: The development target exceeds 85% carbon-based SAF yield using tailored catalysts and in-process stream recycling.
